title: Spot vs Reserved & GPU SKU-aware Routing with Soft Budget Caps
creator: Evan Park
description:
Problem: Customers want predictable cost ceilings while still taking advantage of cheaper spot/preemptible capacity and selecting optimal GPU SKUs for different workloads (memory-heavy vs compute-heavy). Current routing only considers model compatibility and regional latency; it lacks fine-grained cost guards and GPU SKU awareness.

Goal: Implement a policy layer that balances cost and SLOs by: (1) preference ranking between spot, reserved, and on-demand capacity; (2) GPU SKU selection rules (e.g., A100-80GB for KV-heavy/long-seq, H100 for throughput-bound workloads); (3) soft budget caps that throttle or reroute lower-priority requests when a budget window is exceeded; (4) graceful fallback to cheaper model variants or lower-sequence-length execution paths when capacity or budget constraints are hit.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Preemptible/spot instances are cheaper but can be reclaimed; routing must react within 1s for in-flight requests and avoid SLO violations.
- GPU SKU selection must consider memory footprint (KV cache size), supported quantization kernels, and per-token cost.
- Soft budget caps should avoid hard failures: prefer rate-limited degradation paths (lower-cost model / quantized variant / shorter max_tokens) before returning errors.
- Metrics and observability must surface per-customer budget burn, per-route cost, and preemption-induced retries.

Success metrics:
- 10-25% reduction in average cost-per-token for eligible workloads without increasing P95 latency by more than 10%.
- <1% increase in error rate due to routing decisions across active customers.
- Clear dashboard for budget burn + automatic notifications when soft caps trigger.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine implements weighted preference for capacity types: spot > reserved > on-demand with configurable weights
Routing honors GPU SKU constraints and selects compatible SKUs for pinned models
Soft budget cap feature triggers non-disruptive degradation paths (reroute to cheaper model variant, reduce max_tokens, or apply rate limit) rather than hard failures
Observable metrics emitted per request: chosen_capacity_type, chosen_gpu_sku, budget_window_id, budget_remaining_cents
Integration tests simulate spot eviction and validate graceful fallback within 1s for in-flight requests
Runbook and rollout playbook created and reviewed by SRE and Product
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial scoping meeting with Product (Anya Patel) and SRE. Agreed on soft cap semantics and prioritized non-disruptive degradation over errors.
2026-02-18: Design doc drafted (link below). Decision: express routing policies as YAML policies evaluated on request metadata and historical spot reclaim risk.
2026-02-25: Prototype policy evaluator merged to feature branch. Implemented capacity preference and simple GPU SKU matcher. PR: #4127
2026-03-03: Benchmarked prototype on canary traffic: spot preference saved ~18% cost for CPU-bound chat workload; H100 selection improved throughput 12% for throughput tests.
2026-03-08: Implemented soft cap fallback order: 1) route to quantized variant, 2) apply per-route rate limit, 3) shorten max_tokens, 4) route to on-demand. Need UX hooks for PM to tune thresholds.
2026-03-10: Added metrics: routing.choice, budget.window, budget.burn_cents. Drafted runbook. Preparing canary rollout to 5% of read-only tenant traffic week of 2026-03-15.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary (developer traffic) for 48h. 2) 5% tenant canary for read-only/low-priority tenants (monitor cost, latency, error increase). 3) Incremental ramp to 25% with SRE on-call. 4) Full enablement with opt-out flag per-customer and UI in Console to tune soft cap thresholds.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Opting for soft caps reduces customer-visible errors but can hide cost spikes if thresholds are too permissive. We will add alerts for sustained soft-cap activation.
For preemption handling, we prefer retry-on-different-capacity over immediate model fallback for short-lived preemptions; this reduces quality regressions for chat completions.
GPU SKU selection must be deterministic for caching benefits. We will memoize SKU choices per model/route for 1h to stabilize kernel selection and KV cache behavior.
We will start with static SKU compatibility matrix and evolve to a learned cost model once we have 6 weeks of data.
implementation_notes:
Policy YAML example (stored in config store):
---
policy_name: cost-aware-default
priority: 100
capacity_preferences:
  - type: spot
    weight: 0.7
  - type: reserved
    weight: 0.2
  - type: on_demand
    weight: 0.1
gpu_rules:
  - model_tag: kv-heavy
    allowed_skus: [A100-80GB, A100-40GB]
  - model_tag: throughput
    allowed_skus: [H100, A800]
soft_budget_caps:
  window: 1h
  threshold_cents: 5000
  fallback_sequence: [quantized_variant, rate_limit_20pct, reduce_max_tokens_25pct, on_demand]
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for evaluator and SKU matcher
- Integration tests for soft-cap fallback sequence
- Chaos test: simulate spot eviction and confirm graceful fallback within 1s
- Load test at 2x normal traffic to validate SLO impact
risks: Spot eviction cascades causing retries if many in same AZ: mitigate by cross-AZ preference and retry jitter
Over-eager fallback may mask model quality regressions for customers: add audit logs and evals for all fallback responses
communication: Status updates to #runtime-team and weekly sync with Product. Notify customers in advance for canary via Console banner and support emails.
